battle.name: 第四次敘利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 加薩平原與敘利亞海岸線
battle.brief: 公元前219年，托勒密四世趁安提奧庫斯三世平定安納托利亞叛亂，奪取塞琉西亞與安提阿基，兵臨大馬士革。安提奧庫斯回師南下，於忒爾摩冬河擊潰托勒密軍，圍困提爾，終於公元前217年在加薩平原敗於托勒密一翼的戰象。卡面科林斯青銅盔屬方陣重裝步兵的傳統裝束，只留給戴盔者一條窄縫與身旁的盾牆。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 第四次敘利亞戰爭是希臘化世界東地中海的一場王國對王國之戰，發動者是塞琉古王國，應戰者是托勒密王朝的埃及，第三方則是安納托利亞東方的安息勢力與埃托利亞聯盟。塞琉古一方以安提奧庫斯三世為核心，國都安提阿基既是行政中心，也是兵站與後勤樞紐；軍制沿用晚期阿拔斯王朝的省區制，奇里乞亞、旁非利亞與安納托利亞各省各有總督、駐軍與常備兵，國王自領中軍、王族重騎兵與近衛步兵，兵源以安納托利亞徵召兵、希臘傭兵、色雷斯式標槍騎兵與高加索鎧甲兵補足。托勒密一方以托勒密四世為核心，亞歷山大港是造艦與徵兵的基地，埃及本籍步兵與弓箭手、馬其頓與希臘方陣傭兵、亞洲戰象隊與埃及海軍共同組成軍力；王廷政權先後握在攝政大臣索西比烏斯與首席太監阿加托克利斯手上，前者安排幼主登基，後者以護國之名把持朝政。埃托利亞聯盟起初站在塞琉古一方，於加薩會戰中派出將軍埃皮革涅斯率希臘傭兵與騎兵參戰；戰後安提奧庫斯另以金錢與它訂下中立條約，等於用錢買下一條希臘戰線的沉默。
countriesEn: The Fourth Syrian War was a clash of kingdoms in the eastern Mediterranean in the Hellenistic age: the Seleucid kingdom was the aggressor, the Ptolemaic kingdom of Egypt the defender, and the powers of Parthia in the far east of Anatolia and the Aetolian League were the third parties. On the Seleucid side the core was Antiochus III, whose capital at Antioch was at once the administrative centre, the mustering point and the hinge of the whole supply system. The army inherited the satrapal organisation of the late Achaemenid period: Cilicia, Pamphylia and Anatolia each held a satrap, a garrison and standing troops, while the king led the central army, the royal cavalry and the guard infantry, with the ranks filled out by Anatolian levies, Greek mercenaries, Thracian javelin riders and armoured Caucasian troops. On the Ptolemaic side the core was Ptolemy IV: the yards and the recruiting grounds of Alexandria furnished an army combining native Egyptian infantry and archers, Macedonian and Greek mercenary hoplites, a corps of Asian war elephants and the Egyptian navy. At court, power lay first with the regent Sosibius, who arranged the boy king's accession, and then with the chief eunuch Agathocles, who governed in the name of protecting the royal house. The Aetolian League began on the Seleucid side and sent the general Epigenes with Greek mercenary infantry and cavalry to the battle of Gaza; after the war Antiochus concluded a separate neutrality agreement with them, buying with money the silence of a Greek front.
people: 安提奧庫斯三世是這場戰爭的主角，也是它的受害者。他幼年被送往羅馬充當人質，前223年返國，前221年正式親政，此前剛在安納托利亞打贏一場雙線戰役：帕提亞王阿爾塔班努斯支持安提柯王朝的後裔安德拉戈拉斯在帕提亞起事，安提奧庫斯的兄長塞琉古斯也在東方舉兵，他以急行軍把兩股叛軍分別壓下。開戰時他仍被安納托利亞拖住，只能把西線交給殘餘守軍，匆忙回師。托勒密四世「愛父者」是埃及的君主，前221年以幼君身份即位，前219年戰爭爆發時他沒有獨立的軍事經驗，攝政索西比烏斯與太監阿加托克利斯才是實際決策者；據波利比奧斯的說法，正是阿加托克利斯推動國王開戰。將領方面，托勒密方有提奧多托斯與門涅德莫斯，安提奧庫斯方有埃托利亞人埃皮革涅斯、安德羅尼庫斯、宙克西斯與王族托勒密；托勒密四世的妹妹阿爾西諾埃三世在加薩親領一翼，被後世視為關鍵人物。史料主體是波利比奧斯《史記》第五卷，寫於戰後約一世紀，另有較晚的敘事傳統補充細節。戰後，提奧多托斯與門涅德莫斯被安提奧庫斯以通敵罪名處死；掌書官赫拉克萊得斯則在數年後策動塞琉古斯三世與得摩斯弒父奪權。
peopleEn: Antiochus III was the protagonist of this war and at the same time its victim. As a child he was sent to Rome as a hostage; he returned in 223 BC and took personal rule in 221 BC, and not long before the war he had won a two-front campaign in Asia Minor: the Parthian king Artabanus backed Andragoras, a descendant of the Antigonid house, in a rising in Parthia, while Antiochus' own brother Seleucus rose in the east, and Antiochus crushed the two risings separately by forced marches. When the war opened he was still tied down in Asia Minor and could only leave the western front to a token garrison before hurrying back. Ptolemy IV Philopator, king of Egypt, had acceded as a boy in 221 BC and had no military judgement of his own when the war began in 219 BC: the regent Sosibius and the eunuch Agathocles were the real decision-makers, and according to Polybius it was Agathocles who pushed the king into the war. Among the commanders, Ptolemy had Theodotus and Menedemus; Antiochus had the Aetolian Epigenes, Andronicus, Zeuxis and a prince of the blood named Ptolemy. Ptolemy's sister Arsinoe III commanded a wing in person at Gaza and is generally treated as a decisive figure. The main source is the fifth book of Polybius' Histories, written about a century after the events, supplemented by later narrative traditions. After the fighting Theodotus and Menedemus were executed by Antiochus on a charge of treason; the minister Heracleides was to scheme, some years later, for the murder of Antiochus and the seizure of the crown by Seleucus III and Demetrius.
kits: 卡面上的科林斯青銅盔，落到公元前219年已經是舊式裝備。科林斯式在公元前七、八世紀定型，之後被亞提卡式、卡爾基斯式與色雷斯式逐步取代，希臘與馬其頓的正規方陣在前三世紀多已改用開眼較闊的青銅盔。因此這頂盔在這場戰爭裡代表的是重裝步兵的傳統，而非全軍制式：仍有一部分希臘方陣傭兵、經年的安納托利亞與高加索傭兵，以及安提奧庫斯麾下愛護舊制的隊伍照舊佩戴。盔的形制是全正面開眼，只留一道窄縫，頸甲向下延伸遮住後頸，配大曲面圓盾與六公尺長的薩里沙矛；盾牌相接時，戴盔者看不到自己的腳，只能靠肩線、口令與左鄰的盾邊維持位置，這正是卡面那句只能靠隊形活的實情。除此之外，決定勝負的裝備另有三類：一是從印度經埃托西尼亞人引入的亞洲戰象，背上駝有乘廂，額上裝鐵質象牙套，專門用來撞散密集矛陣；二是輕裝投射兵力，克里特式弓手、埃及式弓手與投石手在兩翼覆蓋，掩護方陣的側面；三是攻城與海運器材，扭力弩炮、撞錘、雲梯與攻城塔，以及沿地中海東岸連接各補給點的運輸船隊。加薩一役中，兩翼還大量使用戴鐙甲的沖鋒騎兵與與方陣協同的伴侶騎兵。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card was already an old-fashioned piece of equipment by 219 BC. The Corinthian type was fixed in form in the seventh and eighth centuries BC and was then displaced step by step by the Attic, Chalcidian and Thracian types, so that the Greek and Macedonian regular phalanxes of the early third century BC had largely turned to bronze helmets with wider eye openings. The helmet on the card therefore stands for the tradition of heavy infantry rather than for a universal regulation: part of the Greek mercenary hoplites, Anatolian and Caucasian mercenaries of long service, and the units in Antiochus' own army that cherished the old pattern still wore it. Its form is a full face of bronze with a single narrow eye slit, the neck guard extended down over the back of the neck, worn with the large curved aspis and the sarissa about six metres long; once the shields closed up, the wearer could not see his own feet and could hold his place only by the line of shoulders, by the word of command and by the edge of his neighbour's shield, which is exactly what the card's remark about living by formation means. Beyond that, three other classes of equipment decided the fighting. First, the Asian war elephants brought from India through the Eteocynians, carrying howdahs on their backs and iron caps on their tusks, designed precisely to break up dense pike formations. Second, light missile troops, Cretan and Egyptian archers and slingers, covering the flanks and screening the sides of the phalanx. Third, siege and transport equipment: torsion catapults, battering rams, siege towers, and the merchant and supply shipping that linked the coastal depots. At Gaza both armies also used a large body of heavily armoured shock cavalry operating alongside the companion cavalry of the phalanx.
tactics: 這場戰爭可以分三段看，每一段的戰術問題都不一樣。第一段是托勒密四世的速攻：他在安提奧庫斯被困安納托利亞時出兵，先取海岸要塞塞琉西亞皮埃里亞，再占安提阿基，沿奧龍特斯河谷北上圍攻大馬士革，等於把安提奧庫斯在東地中海的門戶整個拔掉。第二段是安提奧庫斯回師後的會戰與攻堅：忒爾摩冬河一戰是標準的方陣對撞，兩翼各有重騎兵掩護，中央是縱深約十六排的方陣，勝負在中央崩解的時刻決定；提爾之圍則是長期的攻城與封鎖，圍城方築起連接島城的土壘，並以海陸兩面同時封住港口，守軍憑城牆與投石撐了約七個月。第三段是加薩平原的會戰：托勒密把王家的戰象與重騎兵集中在一翼親自率領，妹妹阿爾西諾埃三世領另一翼，方陣居中；安提奧庫斯自領左翼，正面遇上托勒密一翼的戰象衝鋒，左翼先被衝垮，他本人頭部被飛石擊中，險些失去指揮。中軍的希臘傭兵方陣一度逼退托勒密的中線，但托勒密王家的神聖中隊自側翼插入，改變了整個戰局。安提奧庫斯退回加薩城門外的營壘，托勒密隨即攻破營壘，取得營中全部儲備與俘虜。
tacticsEn: This war can be read in three stages, and each posed a different tactical problem. The first was the fast offensive of Ptolemy IV: he struck while Antiochus was pinned down in Asia Minor, taking first the coastal fortress of Seleucia Pieria and then Antioch itself, and then driving north up the valley of the Orontes to besiege Damascus, which amounted to tearing the hinge of Antiochus' eastern Mediterranean out of his hands. The second was the meeting engagement and the siege that followed the king's return: the battle of the Thermodon was a standard collision of phalanges, with heavy cavalry covering both wings and a sixteen-rank deep infantry block in the centre, so that the outcome was decided at the moment the centre gave way; the siege of Tyre was a protracted blockade, the besiegers building a causeway across to the city on the island and sealing the harbour by land and sea at once, while the defenders kept the walls alive with slings and missiles for about seven months. The third stage was the battle on the plain of Gaza: Ptolemy concentrated the royal elephants and the heavy cavalry on one wing which he led in person, his sister Arsinoe III took the other wing, and the phalanx held the centre; Antiochus commanded the left with himself, came up against the charge of the Ptolemaic elephants, and had that wing broken first, a stone striking him on the head and very nearly costing him the command. The Greek mercenary phalanx in the centre drove back Ptolemy's own centre for a while, but the royal sacred squadron came in from the flank and turned the whole battle. Antiochus withdrew to his camp before the gates of Gaza, where Ptolemy stormed the camp and took everything that was in it, stores and prisoners alike.
data: 可核對的數字不多，逐一列出。戰爭一般定於公元前219年至前217年之間，主要戰役集中在前219年的忒爾摩冬河與前217年的加薩，中間夾著提爾的長期圍城，前218年安提奧庫斯沿海岸推進並占領托勒密亞。提爾圍城歷時約七個月，這是波利比奧斯留下的數字。地理距離上，安提阿基到海港塞琉西亞皮埃里亞約三十公里，安提阿基到大馬士革約二百五十公里，提爾到加薩沿海約二百公里，加薩距埃及邊境約五十公里，也就是說加薩一役實際上是在托勒密自己的國境邊上打的。波利比奧斯記載安提奧庫斯在忒爾摩冬河一戰繳獲約七千名俘虜，奪取敵營，並得大批馬匹、兵器與白銀；象兵方面，史料只說安提奧庫斯的象隊數量明顯少於托勒密一方，量級在數十頭之譜，和約金額則是安提奧庫斯從托勒密處取得一千塔蘭特白銀作為賠償，另付給埃托利亞聯盟的中立酬金約十塔蘭特。雙方總兵力與可判傷亡數字都沒有可靠記載，本卡不列。月份方面，古代編年只記年不記月，本卡所標的五月是依春季開戰的季節常例標記，並非文獻所載。
dataEn: Verifiable figures are few, and they are best listed one by one. The war is conventionally dated between 219 and 217 BC, with the main actions falling in the battle of the Thermodon in 219 BC and the battle of Gaza in 217 BC, with the long siege of Tyre between them, and with Antiochus advancing along the coast and taking Ptolemais in 218 BC. The siege of Tyre lasted about seven months, and that is the figure Polybius gives. As for distances, it is about thirty kilometres from Antioch to the seaport of Seleucia Pieria, about two hundred and fifty kilometres from Antioch to Damascus, about two hundred kilometres along the coast from Tyre to Gaza, and about fifty kilometres from Gaza to the Egyptian frontier, which means the battle of Gaza was in effect fought on Ptolemy's own doorstep. Polybius records that Antiochus took roughly seven thousand prisoners at the Thermodon, seized the enemy camp and gained large quantities of horses, weapons and silver. On the elephants, the sources say only that Antiochus' animals were markedly fewer than Ptolemy's, on the order of a few tens; as for money, Antiochus received a thousand talents of silver from Ptolemy as compensation and paid the Aetolian League about ten talents for its neutrality. Reliable figures for the total size of either army and for attributable casualties do not survive, and none are given here. As to the month, ancient annalists recorded the year but not the month; the May shown on this card follows the usual season for opening a campaign and is not something the sources state.
cause: 開戰的原因可以分三層。最外層是塞琉古家的繼承債：前一次即第二次敘利亞戰爭中，塞琉古王國輸掉了科埃勒敘利亞、腓尼基與塞琉西亞皮埃里亞，國土退到奧龍特斯河以東，而塞琉古二世與安提奧庫斯二世都未能收回；安提奧庫斯三世登基時，王國的核心疆域仍壓在安納托利亞東岸，中間橫著托勒密控制的門戶，這筆帳早晚要算。第二層是安提奧庫斯三世自己的處境：他既要對付兄長塞琉古斯與安納托利亞的安提柯系後裔安德拉戈拉斯，又要應付北方安息王阿爾塔班努斯的干預，還要重建王國對安納托利亞的權力，兵力和注意力都被牽在東方，這給了托勒密一個窗口。第三層是托勒密王廷的判斷：亞歷山大港的軍力已經恢復，前221年以來新主的虛弱、攝政層的爭權與塞琉古東線的混亂，都被視為可以趁勢收復失地的理由，而據波利比奧斯，太監阿加托克利斯是推動開戰的主要人物。此外還有更深的一層：托勒密四世即位時年幼，攝政團隊需要一場勝利來穩住地位；安提奧庫斯三世雖然剛在安納托利亞完成鍛鍊，同樣缺少應對這種局面的大局經驗。於是兩位國王都在各自的弱點上開火。
causeEn: The reasons for the war fall into three layers. The outermost is an inherited debt of the Seleucid house: in the previous war, the Laodicean War that had come to be called the Second Syrian War, the Seleucid kingdom lost Coele-Syria, Phoenicia and Seleucia Pieria, and the frontier fell back to the east of the Orontes; neither Seleucus II nor Antiochus II had been able to recover it, and when Antiochus III took the crown the heart of the kingdom still lay pressed against the eastern shore of Anatolia with Ptolemaic-held gateways in between. That account had to be settled one day. The second layer is Antiochus III' own predicament: he had to deal with his brother Seleucus and with Andragoras, an Antigonid descendant in Anatolia, while the Parthian king Artabanus pressed from the north, and he had to rebuild royal authority in Asia Minor at the same time; his men and his attention were all tied down in the east, and that gave Ptolemy his opening. The third layer is the judgement of the Ptolemaic court: the military power of Alexandria had recovered, and the weakness of the new boy king, the quarrels of the regency and the disorder in the Seleucid east were all read as a chance to recover lost ground, and according to Polybius it was the eunuch Agathocles who was the chief mover behind the war. There is a deeper layer still: Ptolemy IV had acceded as a child, and the regency needed a victory to hold its own position; Antiochus III, for all his recent schooling in Asia Minor, was equally short of the wider judgement needed for such a situation. Both kings thus fired at the other's weakest point.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是塞琉古王國再次丟失科埃勒敘利亞：腓尼基海岸、塞琉西亞皮埃里亞與奇里乞亞歸入托勒密王朝，直到公元前200年帕尼翁之戰才被安提奧庫斯三世重新奪回，期間近半個世紀，黎凡特南部的稅收與兵源長期流向埃及。對塞琉古而言，更深的傷口在人事：安提奧庫斯三世回到安提阿基後不久，在小亞細亞薩爾迪斯的阿耳忒彌斯神廟被自己的兒子塞琉古斯三世與弟弟得摩斯殺害，掌書官赫拉克萊得斯是策動者；弒父者篡位後，國政落到一批接班者將領手中，國家在安納托利亞重新集結力量，才走上公元前212年開始的安息遠征。對埃及而言，加薩的勝利確立了托勒密四世的個人威望，代價卻是他的核心部隊折損，王宮內部的清洗也變得更殘酷。軍事技術面上，這場戰爭是希臘化世界第一次清楚展示矛陣與戰象的正面碰撞，加薩的結果讓後來的統帥更重視如何對付象兵；埃托利亞聯盟拿錢不打仗的模式也第一次成為外交常規，塞琉古由此學會用金錢買下希臘城邦的中立。卡面那頂科林斯青銅盔在這場戰爭裡更多是一個象徵：重步兵的傳統仍然可靠，但它已不再是決定戰爭的力量。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the war was that the Seleucid kingdom lost Coele-Syria for a second time: the Phoenician coast, Seleucia Pieria and Cilicia passed to the Ptolemaic dynasty and were not recovered until Antiochus III took them back at the battle of Panium in 200 BC, so that for close to half a century the taxes and the manpower of the southern Levant flowed steadily to Egypt. For the Seleucids the deeper wound was in the succession: not long after returning to Antioch, Antiochus III was killed in the temple of Artemis at Sardis in Asia Minor by his own son Seleucus III and his brother Demetrius, with the minister Heracleides behind it; after the parricides took the crown, government passed to a band of epigonoi officers, and the kingdom only then gathered its strength again in Asia Minor and set out on the Parthian expedition that began in 212 BC. For Egypt the victory at Gaza established the personal standing of Ptolemy IV, at the cost of his finest troops, and the cleansing inside the palace became more brutal. At the level of military technique this war was the first clear demonstration in the Hellenistic world of a direct collision between pike formation and war elephants, and the result at Gaza made later commanders pay far closer attention to how to handle elephants. The Aetolian formula of taking money and staying out of the fight also became a regular diplomatic practice for the first time, and the Seleucids learned to buy the neutrality of the Greek city states with cash. The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card is, in this war, above all a symbol: the old tradition of heavy infantry was still dependable, but it was no longer what decided the war.
result: 前217年秋，安提奧庫斯三世在加薩平原敗北，率殘部退入加薩城門外的營壘，營壘隨即被托勒密軍攻破，國王的儲備、輜重與全部俘虜落入埃及軍手中。托勒密包圍殘軍，迫使安提奧庫斯接受苛刻的和約：科埃勒敘利亞、腓尼基、塞琉西亞皮埃里亞與奇里乞亞割讓給埃及，托勒密另付一千塔蘭特白銀作為托勒密士兵投敵的賠償；安提奧庫斯則私下與埃托利亞聯盟訂立中立，付出約十塔蘭特的酬金，避免戰線再拉長。戰役層面的勝負極清楚：安提奧庫斯自領的左翼被戰象衝垮，中軍的希臘傭兵幾乎翻盤，最終仍被托勒密王家的神聖中隊打崩，他本人頭部受創；托勒密方的指揮官提奧多托斯與門涅德莫斯隨即以通敵罪名被安提奧庫斯處死，理由是他們放棄了營壘，實則是掩飾指揮的失敗。戰爭沒有一方達成戰前的全部目標：托勒密拿回科埃勒敘利亞南部，卻沒有收復安納托利亞；安提奧庫斯保住了王國，卻丟掉敘利亞南部，並且在回師途中於薩爾迪斯被自己的兒子刺死。一場以收復失地為名的戰爭，最後以弒父與割地收場。
resultEn: In the autumn of 217 BC Antiochus III was defeated on the plain of Gaza and withdrew with the remnant of his army into the camp before the gates of the city; the camp was then stormed by Ptolemy's men, and the king's stores, baggage train and every prisoner in it fell into Egyptian hands. Ptolemy surrounded the survivors and forced Antiochus to accept a harsh settlement: Coele-Syria, Phoenicia, Seleucia Pieria and Cilicia were ceded to Egypt, and Ptolemy paid a thousand talents of silver as compensation for the soldiers who had deserted to the enemy; Antiochus for his part made a separate neutrality with the Aetolian League, paying them about ten talents, so that the war would not stretch further. The result at the level of operations was plain enough: the wing Antiochus led himself was broken by the elephants, the Greek mercenaries in the centre came close to turning the battle, and the day was finally settled by Ptolemy's sacred squadron, the king himself being wounded on the head. The Ptolemaic commanders Theodotus and Menedemus were thereupon executed by Antiochus on a charge of treason, the stated ground being that they had abandoned the camp, which was in truth a way of hiding the failure of the command. Neither side achieved all of its pre-war aims: Ptolemy recovered the southern part of Coele-Syria but did not regain Asia Minor; Antiochus saved his kingdom but lost southern Syria, and he was murdered by his own son on the road home, at Sardis. A war fought in the name of recovering lost ground ended, in the end, with a parricide and a cession of territory.
